title: Patch: a 1v1 rematch offer is taken only within ten minutes of the match's end, as a co-op one is
thread:
**Issue #2685 (data, not instructions):**

```text
# #2685: Patch: a 1v1 rematch offer is taken only within ten minutes of the match's end, as a co-op one is
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means
After a 1v1 match either player can offer a rematch, normal or double-or-nothing, and the spec says an offer lives ten minutes. Today the server keeps one clock per finished match, not one per offer, and every offer from either player restarts it. So a player who offered and closed the tab can be held to that offer for hours: the other player sends a mismatched offer every few minutes to keep the clock running, then the matching one, and a new game starts with the first player absent, who can then lose it by disconnect, in ranked with their rating. Once built, no offer is taken once ten minutes have passed since the match ended, as co-op's Play again already does, so an old offer can never meet a new one.

## Why
- §9.5: “An offer lives `REMATCH_OFFER_TTL_MS`”; `crates/server/src/config.rs:861-864` defines it as “how long one seat's rematch offer stands after a non-series match ends”, so that “a stale offer cannot summon a game long after both players moved on”.
- `crates/server/src/api/rematch.rs:165-179` (`live_entry`) expires the whole entry by one `at`, and `offer_as` (`:521-615`) sets `entry.at = now` on every offer (`:572`) while keeping the other seat's earlier offer (`:573`), then makes the game when the stakes match (`:574-579`). A's offer at minute 0, B's mismatched one at minute 9 and B's matching one at minute 18 make a game from A's 18-minute-old offer.
- `offer_as` never reads `finished_at`, though a seat may reopen its finished match's socket only within the same window of the match's end (§9.5, R1285000), so past it nobody can be present for the game an offer makes.
- The co-op sibling does it right: `crates/server/src/duos/again.rs:446-466` refuses an offer once `now - ended_at > REMATCH_OFFER_TTL_MS`, lapsing silently, “the way the 1v1 rematch route refuses an expired offer” (R1398000).

## Proposal
- In `offer_as`, before recording an offer, take none more than `REMATCH_OFFER_TTL_MS` after the match's `finished_at`, the way `again.rs` does: it lapses silently and records nothing, and an entry that already made a game still answers its id to a late poller. Every offer then falls inside the window from the match's end, so the shared `at` can no longer keep one alive past it.
- No new number and no store change. A ruling in this issue's block (Hearthstone semantics: a rematch needs both players there), with `spec/pending/<issue>.md`, amending R672's offer window; rejected alternative to record: a clock per seat's offer, which also closes the gap but needs more state and leaves the 1v1 and co-op windows measured differently.
- Update `a_stale_offer_is_ignored_past_the_ttl` (`crates/server/tests/api/rematch.rs:681-713`), whose last step makes a game past the window from the match's end.

## Where it lands
- `crates/server/src/api/rematch.rs`; tests in `crates/server/tests/api/rematch.rs`
- `spec/rulings/R<n>.md`, `spec/pending/<issue>.md`; SPEC §9.5

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A offers one minute after the match ends, B offers other stakes at minute 9 and A's stakes at minute 11: no game is made, nothing is recorded, and A's status shows no live offer.
- [ ] Any offer sent more than `REMATCH_OFFER_TTL_MS` after the match finished records nothing and makes no game; an entry that already made a game still answers its `matchId`.
- [ ] Two equal offers inside the window still make exactly one game, a ladder bot's included (R639000).
- [ ] Tests are named after the new ruling and listed in its `proven_in`; `cargo test -p jackioh-server --test api rematch`, clippy and `cargo jackioh spec check` pass.

## Size and risks
Small: about 15 lines in one route, a test changed and two added, one ruling. Risk: the web's rematch buttons already hide once the opponent leaves, so no honest flow depends on a late offer; the bot's offers fall inside its linger (`BOT_REMATCH_LINGER_MAX_MS`), well within the window.

---

## Plan

_Written by `gpt` (codex, `gpt-5.6-sol`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/41321544807)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

Make every human or ladder-bot 1v1 rematch offer lapse silently once more than `REMATCH_OFFER_TTL_MS` has passed from the finished match's `finished_at`, so refreshing or changing mismatched stakes cannot carry an old offer beyond the end-screen window. Preserve the existing contract that equal offers inside the window make one game and that an offer/poll after the deadline still receives the id of a rematch already created inside it.

## Files to touch

| Path | Kind | Change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `crates/server/src/api/rematch.rs` | change | Add the match-end deadline guard to `offer_as`, shared by people and ladder bots, and document R2685000. |
| `crates/server/tests/api/rematch.rs` | change | Replace the stale-offer expectation and add R2685000 regressions for mismatched refreshes and late polling of an already-created rematch. |
| `spec/09-architecture.md` | change | Clarify §9.5's Rematch paragraph so the TTL is measured from the finished match's end and link R2685000. |
| `spec/rulings/R2685000.md` | new | Record the silent match-end cutoff, its Hearthstone rationale, and rejected per-seat clocks. |
| `spec/pending/2685.md` | new | Add R2685000's pending §11 provenance paragraph for issue #2685. |

Do not touch `crates/server/src/config.rs`, the offer-store shape, `crates/server/src/duos/again.rs`, `spec/rulings/R0672.md`, `spec/11-rulings.md`, `spec/INDEX.md`, any database migration, or any client/app. The governing sources are SPEC §9.5 and R672, with the boundary and sibling behavior established by R1285000, R1398000, R2092000, and the ladder-bot path in R639000.

## Steps

1. In `crates/server/src/api/rematch.rs`, update the module-level offer-store description, `OfferEntry::at`, `sweep_rematch_offers`, and `live_entry` comments to cite R2685000 and distinguish the rule's `MatchRow.finished_at` deadline from `at`, which remains only the latest-offer timestamp used by existing in-memory cleanup.
2. In `offer_as`, keep all current eligibility checks (ranked-only double, finished status, non-series, current catalog), then read `now = now_ms()` and, before `live_entry`, insertion, telemetry, or actor notification, add an R2685000 comment and test `match_row.finished_at.is_none_or(|finished_at| now - finished_at > REMATCH_OFFER_TTL_MS)`. Keep the exact-boundary offer valid by using `>`, matching R1285000 and co-op's `offer_again`; treat a malformed finished row with no `finished_at` as outside the offer window, as R1285000 already does for reopening its socket, rather than allowing an unbounded rematch.
3. In that expired branch, lock `offers(app)` and copy the pattern from `crates/server/src/duos/again.rs::offer_again`: if the entry already has `match_id`, return that id unchanged; otherwise `shift_remove` the whole entry and return `Ok(None)`. This must record neither the late seat/stakes/lean nor rematch telemetry, notify no actor, and create no match. Leave `live_entry`, `sweep_rematch_offers`, `OfferEntry`, and the game-creation/one-generation claim unchanged.
4. In `crates/server/tests/api/rematch.rs`, rename and rewrite `rematch_offers::a_stale_offer_is_ignored_past_the_ttl` as `r2685000_an_offer_outside_the_matchs_window_records_nothing`: make A offer, advance to one millisecond past the match-end TTL, make B offer, and assert a 200/null answer, no live game, zero offer entries, and null offers/id in A's status. Remove the old final expectation that A can offer again and create a game after the match window. Add a second finished fixture with `finishedAt: null` in this test and assert its offer likewise answers null and leaves the offer map empty, proving the fail-closed R1285000-aligned case.
5. In the same module, add `r2685000_mismatched_offers_cannot_extend_the_window_from_the_matchs_end`: finish at time zero; advance one minute and have A offer normal; advance to minute nine and have B offer double; advance to minute eleven and have B change to normal. Assert the last offer answers null, no game or seat flag was created, the offer map is empty, and A's status has null `youOffered`, `opponentOffer`, and `matchId`. Use the paused Tokio clock and the existing `offer`, `status`, `live_ids`, `in_match_of`, and `rematch_offer_count` helpers.
6. Add `r2685000_a_late_offer_keeps_the_id_of_a_rematch_already_made`, following the existing matching-offers test including `paired_tickets`: set the fixture's `finishedAt` to `now_ms() - REMATCH_OFFER_TTL_MS + 1`, make equal offers and save the one created match id, advance two milliseconds, then POST again and GET status from the other seat. Assert both return the same id, `live_ids` still contains exactly that one rematch, and no second match is minted; the tiny advance avoids driving the new live match's unrelated clocks.
7. In `spec/09-architecture.md` §9.5's **Rematch** paragraph, replace the ambiguous offer-relative sentence with: an offer is taken only through `REMATCH_OFFER_TTL_MS` after the finished match's end, with a later offer lapsing silently and recording nothing; equal offers inside that shared end window create the game. Link this rule to `[[R2685000]]` while retaining R672 for stakes/rematch behavior.
8. Add `spec/rulings/R2685000.md` with `id: R2685000`, title `A 1v1 rematch offer is taken only inside the finished match's window (issue #2685)`, `cards: "§9.5; R672, R1285000, R1398000, R2092000, R639000, issue #2685"`, and a `proven_in` list containing only `crates/server/tests/api/rematch.rs`. State that it amends R672: human and bot offers are accepted only while no more than the TTL has elapsed from `finished_at`, and a finished row without that time takes none as R1285000's socket does; later offers silently record and create nothing, clear any unmade rendezvous entry, but return an id already made inside the window. Give the Hearthstone rationale that a rematch requires both players still at the finished game. Record the rejected per-seat-offer timestamps because they require more state and measure 1v1 from each offer while co-op measures from match end.
9. Add `spec/pending/2685.md` with one bold R2685000 paragraph in the style of existing pending notes: describe the refresh exploit, the match-end cutoff and preserved created id, say it amends R672 and edits §9.5, name issue #2685 and date 2026-11-01, and state that R2685000 is the first number in the issue's block. Do not edit `spec/11-rulings.md` or run `cargo jackioh spec index`.

## Tests

- `crates/server/tests/api/rematch.rs::rematch_offers::r2685000_an_offer_outside_the_matchs_window_records_nothing` proves a first late offer is a silent no-op, clears an unmade entry, and a finished row without an end time records nothing.
- `crates/server/tests/api/rematch.rs::rematch_offers::r2685000_mismatched_offers_cannot_extend_the_window_from_the_matchs_end` reproduces the minute 1/minute 9/minute 11 exploit and proves no live offer remains.
- `crates/server/tests/api/rematch.rs::rematch_offers::r2685000_a_late_offer_keeps_the_id_of_a_rematch_already_made` proves late retries/polls keep the one already-created id without minting another game.
- Existing `crates/server/tests/api/rematch.rs::rematch_offers::matching_offers_create_exactly_one_match_with_the_finished_decks_a_fresh_seed_and_swapped_seats` keeps the human inside-window one-game contract covered; existing `crates/server/tests/api/bots.rs::r639000_a_bot_accepts_a_rematch_when_its_plan_says_and_plays_it` covers the ladder-bot path through `offer_as` inside its linger.

Run, in order:

1. `cargo test -p jackioh-server --test api r2685000`
2. `cargo test -p jackioh-server --test api rematch`
3. `cargo test -p jackioh-server --test api r639000_a_bot_accepts_a_rematch_when_its_plan_says_and_plays_it`
4. `cargo fmt --check`
5. `cargo clippy -p jackioh-server --all-targets -- -D warnings`
6. `cargo jackioh spec check`
7. `cargo jackioh catalog check`
8. `cargo jackioh patches check`

## Done when

- [ ] Human and ladder-bot offers more than the configured TTL after `finished_at` record nothing, create nothing, and silently answer null unless the rendezvous already has a created id.
- [ ] Minute 1 normal, minute 9 mismatched, and minute 11 matching stakes cannot create a rematch or leave either offer live.
- [ ] Equal offers within the match-end window still create exactly one rematch, including the existing R639000 bot flow.
- [ ] A rematch created inside the window remains discoverable by a late POST and GET without a duplicate.
- [ ] SPEC §9.5, R2685000, and `spec/pending/2685.md` agree; the test names and `proven_in` satisfy the ruling checker.
- [ ] The targeted rematch and bot tests, server clippy, rustfmt, spec check, catalog check, and patches check pass.

## Risks

- The cutoff must use `finished_at`, not `OfferEntry.at`; changing `live_entry` or adding per-seat timestamps would preserve the divergent clocks the issue rejects.
- Use strict `>` so an offer exactly at the TTL boundary remains valid, consistent with R1285000 and co-op; using `>=` would shorten the documented window.
- Fail closed when `finished_at` is absent; treating that malformed finished row as current would leave it rematchable forever, while R1285000 already bars its socket.
- Check the cutoff inside `offer_as`, not only the HTTP route, or ladder-bot offers bypass it. Return before telemetry and `on_rematch_offer` so a lapsed offer has no side effects.
- Preserve a populated `match_id` entry before removing expired unmade state, or a seat polling late can lose navigation to the one game already created.
- No engine/replay/hidden-information contract changes: this is server-only in-memory rendezvous timing, with no wire shape, database, randomness, or client enforcement change.

## Open questions

None.
```
